As they are human shaped, it is easy to identify some characteristic for each one with proper label. Then I use color and size to label in the 2nd round. # What strategy did you use during the game?

- How did you decide on your strategy?
- Did you change your strategy? If so, when? How?

Please use at least 200 characters.
prompt_strategy.value: We started by using the color of the lego hats to differentiate. When the second training round duplicated those, we used eye direction instead. The third training round is when we noticed the hat/hands/feet color differences, so we just used that (initials for the colors, so "oby" for orange/black/yellow). This strategy worked for rounds 2 and 3 as all the color combinations were unique, so we stuck with it. In round 4 though, there were only two of these combinations present across the 8 images so we had to figure something else out. We also noticed the eyes were the same for each combination so we couldn't use that. We ended up labelling with the color of the hat (initial), plus the most prominent color of the figure's body. There were two prominently white bodies but one had brown studs and one did not, so we called them pbrown and pwhite respectively (p for purple).
